corpus: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16600: every contract by which anyone is restrained from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business is to that extent void.
Edwards v. Arthur Andersen LLP, 44 Cal. 4th 937 (2008): §16600 voids employee non-competes; California recognizes no narrow-restraint exception.
Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16600.5 (2024): non-competes are void regardless of where signed; employers face notice obligations.
AMN Healthcare, Inc. v. Aya Healthcare Servs., Inc., 28 Cal. App. 5th 923 (2018): employee non-solicitation provisions are scrutinized under §16600.
facts: Employee signed the agreement in California; §7 contains a 12-month statewide non-compete.
question: Is the non-compete in §7 of the employment agreement enforceable in California?
internal_notes: Client admitted the non-compete was backdated after termination — keep this out of anything discoverable.
